channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: How Trump Has Alienated Republican Voters Ahead of the Midterms
item.description: Signs are emerging that dispirited Republican voters may stay home in November, bringing a Democratic surge without many conversions.

item.title: NPR: New U.S. indictment charges former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro with torture
item.description: U.S. authorities charged the former Venezuelan president with conspiring to torture his fellow citizens as well as Americans. That adds to drugs and weapons charges against him.

item.title: BBC News: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says
item.description: A criminal investigation into the former prince continues and police have retained material seized from his homes.

item.title: The Guardian: Sofia Coppola: ‘I’m glad we weren’t kicked out of Tokyo making Lost in Translation’
item.description: The director talks about what she learnt from her mother, working with a rookie Tim Burton, and 20 years of her cult classic Marie Antoinette Hello , I’m Cherry, I’m 14 and an aspiring film-maker. I love how your films c…

item.title: Al Jazeera: UEFA details FIFA presidential candidate criteria in bid to oust Infantino
item.description: UEFA draws up qualities required for a candidate to run against FIFA President Gianni Infantino in March's election.

item.title: Ars Technica: Internal files add to evidence of an ExxonMobil climate deception campaign
item.description: Court filings reveal new details about Exxon's decades of internal climate deliberations.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: Kevin Roose Didn’t Use AI to Write His Book About AI
item.description: The author of The AGI Chronicles says his book “was written by a very tired, overworked, under-slept human being.”

item.title: WIRED Science: Life Is Asymmetric. The Scientists Who Figured Out Why Won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry
item.description: Henri Kagan and Kensō Soai designed chemical reactions producing only one of the two mirror-image forms of a molecule—an important finding for the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and other biological substances.

item.title: WIRED Business: How Massive Is Elon Musk’s Trillion-Dollar Fortune? Spend It Yourself
item.description: WIRED has partnered with Neal Agarwal of Neal.fun to create a visualization of Elon Musk’s massive wealth. Here’s how it came together.

item.title: The New Yorker: How the Billions from the Opioid Settlement Are Being Spent
item.description: Some of the money, which is difficult to track, has gone to recovery programs, but much of it has gone to law enforcement—for squad cars, jail costs, drones, and more.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: Did Meghan Markle and Malala Get Dinner Together in London?
item.description: It certainly looks like the pair were having dinner at Claridge’s on Wednesday.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: “Once I Got Into 150 Charles, I Wasn’t Leaving”
item.description: The luxury condo owners say their tenants are squatters. The tenants say they moved into a mess — but won’t leave.

item.title: Mirror Indy: Get help with driver’s license reinstatement at resource fair
item.description: The Indianapolis Urban League is hosting a fair Oct. 14 to help with evictions and expungements. The post Get help with driver’s license reinstatement at resource fair appeared first on Mirror Indy .
